subject: Privatelink selection and egress lockdown — network preflight
messages:
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@findata.io>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@findata.io>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:18:00Z
Subject: Follow-up from today's deployment chat — Private VPC questions

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so NetOps can start sizing things:  

- Our preferred deployment model is Private VPC (no hosted API). We want tenant isolation and to keep inference traffic on our network.
- Primary question: PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — we have a compliance constraint that no inference traffic may route through the public internet; which option best satisfies that for your managed control plane?
- CIDR plan: we can allocate a /16 to start (10.4.0.0/16), but need to confirm required ranges for service endpoints and any egress IPs to allowlist.
- We will likely restrict egress: only allow connections to your private endpoints; nothing else out to the internet.

Attached is our first-pass network diagram (finData_network_diagram_v1.pdf). NetOps will need a short checklist of exact ports, protocols, and destination IPs for allowlisting. Also advise if there are any mandatory TLS client certs or mTLS steps for PrivateLink.

Can we get that checklist by EOD Friday? Also looping in our NetOps alias (netops@findata.io) on technical details.

Thanks,
Samir
CTO, FinData
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@findata.io>
Cc: NetOps Team <netops@findata.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-14T10:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's deployment chat — Private VPC questions

Hi Samir — appreciate the clear notes and the diagram. Summary and next steps from our side:  

1) PrivateLink vs Peering: both keep traffic off the public internet, but they have different operational trade-offs. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives stronger control and no route table changes from your side — we recommend PrivateLink when customers need strict egress controls and per-tenant/private endpoints. VPC peering is simpler for high-throughput low-latency workloads but requires CIDR non-overlap and route updates.

2) Allowlist / Egress: We'll provide the minimal set of IPs used by our PrivateLink appliances and a range used for management/control plane callbacks. For strictly locked down environments we typically recommend PrivateLink + customer-side security groups that only permit connections to the interface endpoints.

3) TLS/mTLS: Our PrivateLink supports TLS; mTLS is available as an add-on for enterprise customers. If you need mutual TLS, we can include the certificate exchange step in the onboarding playbook.

Action items (we'll own #2 and #3):
- Priyom: Produce a 1-page preflight checklist (ports, IPs, TTLs) and a short decision table (PrivateLink vs Peering) — deliver by 2026-08-14 17:00 PT.
- Marissa: Assist with contractual notes re: PrivateLink add-on and estimated monthly costs for reserved endpoints.
- Karthik: Prep a brief runbook for NetOps covering CIDR constraints and route/sg examples.

Samir — can you confirm the CIDR you mentioned (10.4.0.0/16) and the internal NetOps contact we should use for any network-level testing (name + phone/email)? Also confirm whether on-prem (air-gapped) is on the table or if this is strictly cloud VPC.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Action checklist and attachments — PrivateLink / Peering decision aid

Samir / NetOps — attached two stubs: rdw_privatelink-vs-peering-cheat-sheet.pdf and a one-page preflight checklist. Highlights below:  

- Recommended: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) given your egress lockdown requirement. Pros: no route table changes, per-endpoint security group control, easier audit trail. Cons: small per-endpoint cost and slight connection setup overhead.
- Required allowlist: 54.162.12.0/24 (control callbacks), 54.162.13.40 (health-check IP), service FQDN: api.redwood-inference.internal. We will provide a signed manifest with final IPs by our EOD deliverable.
- Ports: 443 (TLS) outbound from your VPC to interface endpoints.
- mTLS: available — if you require it we'll schedule a cert exchange.

Attachments: rdw_privatelink-vs-peering-cheat-sheet.pdf, rdw_privatelink_preflight_checklist.pdf

- Marissa -> send pricing note by 2026-08-15.

I'll set a 30-min follow-up on Monday to validate connectivity test results.

Thanks,
Priyom
